meta.title: ExperimentLens — Observability & explainability for agents, LLMs and ML experiments
meta.description: A visual analytics dashboard for agentic and ML systems. Trace agents and LLM apps with Langfuse, score them with judges and checks, compare sessions — then drill into the same runs, metrics and explainability you already track.

agenticHero.titlePost: your agents, LLM apps and ML experiments.
agenticHero.subtitle:
ExperimentLens brings visual analytics to agentic systems.It captures full traces, LLM-as-judge verdicts and deterministic checks for every run — so you can see exactly how your agents retrieve, reason and answer.
Each experiment run links to one or many traces, side by side with the parameters and metrics you already track. It's still the same dashboard for classic ML experiment tracking, comparison and explainability.
agenticHero.imageAlt: ExperimentLens agentic overview dashboard with parallel coordinates plot
agenticHero.imageCaption: ExperimentLens dashboard: analyzing configuration effects on experiment performance.

agenticValueProps.title: See how your agents actually behave.
agenticValueProps.subtitle: From the first span to the final verdict — every run, fully traced and scored.

items.title: End-to-end tracing
items.body: Records every observation — retrievers, LLM calls and judges — with latency, tokens and cost captured per step of the trace.

items.title: Judges & verdicts
items.body: LLM-as-judge scores sit next to deterministic checks like citation validity and exact match — as one pass/fail verdict grid.

items.title: Compare sessions
items.body: Line runs up side by side: judge pass-rates, token usage, cumulative latency races and a verdict diff that flags every regression and fix between configurations.

items.title: Agent performance
items.body: Per-agent latency, call frequency and quality breakdowns reveal which step is slowing you down or dragging quality.

agenticShowcase.title: Traces, verdicts and dashboards — in one lens.
agenticShowcase.subtitle: The same run you launch as an experiment, explorable down to a single LLM call.

cards.title: Cumulative latency race
cards.sub: Where each run spends its time

hero.subtitle:
ExperimentLens is a lightweight yet powerful visual dashboard for the interactive exploration, monitoring, and explainability of complex AI pipelines.
Developed within the context of the ExtremeXP project, ExperimentLens empowers researchers, data scientists, and engineers to make sense of experimental results across multiple runs and interconnected tasks.
hero.imageAlt: ExperimentLens overview dashboard with parallel coordinates plot across 108 runs
hero.imageCaption: ExperimentLens dashboard: analyzing configuration effects on experiment performance.

valueProps.title: A single lens over your entire ML experimentation loop.
valueProps.subtitle: From orchestration to explanation — without leaving the browser.

items.title: Tracker- & engine-agnostic
items.body: Adapter interface to MLflow today, with Kubeflow as the execution engine. Airflow and other backends are on the roadmap.

items.title: Visual analytics, not just tables
items.body: Parallel coordinates, comparative metric views, group-by, filters and color encodings — designed to make 100s of runs legible at a glance.

items.title: Explainability built-in
items.body: Feature importance, Partial Dependence (PDP), Accumulated Local Effects (ALE) and counterfactual views wired directly to your runs.

featuresPreview.title: Built for the whole experiment lifecycle.
featuresPreview.subtitle: From first run to final explanation — everything in one UI.

integrations.title: Works with the stack you already run.
integrations.subtitle: ExperimentLens consumes runs from your tracker, traces from your agent stack, and orchestrates them through your engine.

cards.name: Langfuse
cards.body: Instruments your agents and LLM apps. ExperimentLens reads Langfuse traces directly, so every span, generation, judge and check maps back to the run that produced it.

cards.name: MLflow
cards.body: Logs runs, parameters, metrics and artifacts. ExperimentLens reads MLflow experiments directly so every visualization, comparison and explanation maps back to a real MLflow run.

cards.name: Kubeflow
cards.body: Runs the underlying pipelines on Kubernetes. ExperimentLens surfaces Kubeflow pipeline executions as first-class workflows you can inspect, compare and explain.

integrations.footnote: Adapter-based design — additional trackers and engines (e.g. Airflow) can be added without changing the UI.

howItWorks.title: From pipeline to insight in three steps.

steps.title: Orchestrate
steps.body: Author your experiment as an execution engine pipeline. ExperimentLens picks it up as a first-class workflow.

steps.title: Track
steps.body: Each run logs parameters, metrics and artifacts to the tracker — automatically surfaced in the dashboard.

steps.title: Explore & explain
steps.body: Compare runs visually, drill into artifacts and apply explainability methods without leaving the UI.

demoStrip.title: See it on a real experiment.
demoStrip.subtitle: A public deployment running a 108-run fairness experiment.
